defects.before: - Each loop pass loads 256 B from `sp`, passes the barrier, stores 256 B to `dp`, and moves both pointers by 32 words.

defects.before: Returns `(i + 1)` times a fixed 64-bit constant, then XOR with `salt`. The constant is odd. Two different indexes therefore never give the same value. Each test passes its own `salt` (1 to 4), so the tests use different values for the same word.
defects.after:
- Returns `(i + 1)` times a fixed 64-bit constant, then XOR (bitwise exclusive or, `^`) with `salt`.
- The constant is odd. Two different indexes therefore never give the same value for the same `salt`.
- The file has four fill loops (lines 63, 84, 111 and 120). They pass the salts 1 to 4. So no two fills give a word the same value.
defects.evidence: selftest.c has four fill loops with salts 1 to 4 (lines 63, 84, 111, 120), and the read, copy and write tests of test_block all share salt 3 for page a, so "each test passes its own salt" is false.

defects.before: the second argument of `pattern`. Each test uses its own number, so its fill values differ from the values of the other tests.
defects.after: the second argument of `pattern`. The four fill loops of selftest.c use the numbers 1 to 4, so no two fills give a word the same value.
defects.evidence: Same source lines as above: the three tests of test_block use salt 3 for page a (lines 111, 116, 125, 133), so a salt belongs to a fill loop, not to a test.

defects.evidence: Line 150 of selftest.c sets the three buffer sizes to 1 page, 3 pages and 1 MiB, and test_block uses one page, so "small" had no size.

defects.before: `MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS` means memory of this process only, with no file behind it.
defects.after: `MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS` means memory of this process only. It is not the content of a file.
defects.evidence: "with no file behind it" is a figure of speech (plain-English rule 1); the mmap(2) page of man7.org says for MAP_ANONYMOUS "The mapping is not backed by any file; its contents are initialized to zero."

defects.before: Without this call the lines would wait in a memory buffer, and a `SIGSEGV` would lose them.
defects.after: Without this call the lines would stay in a memory buffer of the process, and they would be lost when a `SIGSEGV` ends the process.
defects.evidence: "lines wait" and "a SIGSEGV loses them" are figures of speech (plain-English rule 1); a small test program in the scratchpad that prints three lines to a file and then reads a PROT_NONE page left a file of 0 bytes without setvbuf and all three lines with `_IOLBF`, with exit status 139 in both cases.
